source_snapshot.procedure: Enter BMC-Web -> Hardware Status -> Inventory and LEDs, then check all Quick links.
source_snapshot.criteria: All Quick links should be workable.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek incorrectly reduces Quick-link navigation to a Redfish Identify/UID LED toggle and physical LED observation.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that every Quick link displayed on the target BMC WebUI Hardware Status > Inventory and LEDs page is usable and routes or opens as intended.
original_test_intent.target: The rendered Quick-link controls on the specified BMC WebUI page for one verified BMC/SUT and firmware/UI build.
original_test_intent.scope: Enumerate and exercise every Quick link shown on that page. The row does not instruct the tester to toggle Identify/UID LEDs or to replace WebUI interaction with a Redfish action.
original_test_intent.operation: Use the actual BMC WebUI, record the baseline link inventory, activate each Quick link one at a time, verify the resulting page/dialog/resource and return to the source page without invoking unrelated controls.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 5 attended and 5 machine minutes; each displayed Quick link is checked once unless the product specification says otherwise.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every displayed Quick link is enabled when applicable, activates without UI/navigation error and opens the destination or function defined by the BMC UI specification on the same intended management target.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: BMC/SUT and UI version, source-page screenshot, complete visible Quick-link list, and per-link label, expected destination, observed destination/dialog, same-target identity, error status and screenshot/browser evidence.
ambiguities: The source does not provide the expected Quick-link inventory or destination matrix.
`Workable` is not defined beyond successful link behavior.
The page title mentions LEDs, but the procedure does not say that a Quick link changes LED state.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly restores full-link coverage, same-target checks and per-link evidence. It still treats an Identify/UID LED action and physical confirmation as part of this row even though the source only says to check Quick links. That assumption could create an unauthorized state change and test behavior outside scope.

applicable_history.decision: V2 rejects DeepSeek's one-LED shortcut and requires all Quick links, but carries the unsupported LED-toggle assumption into the contract. No user ruling establishes an LED-control step for this exact row.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the class because protected WebUI access, a browser/interaction harness and the firmware-specific expected link matrix are normal inputs. Limit the test to the actual WebUI Quick links. A state-changing LED test is excluded unless a later source revision explicitly defines it.

available_now: The WebUI location, action of checking all displayed Quick links and high-level criterion are known.
The rendered link list and observed destinations can be collected once protected BMC WebUI access is provided.
missing_inputs: The BMC/UI owner must provide the firmware-specific Quick-link inventory, expected destination/dialog and role/permission behavior.
The execution owner must provide protected credentials, validated BMC identity/TLS and a compatible browser or approved UI automation package.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BMC firmware/UI owner supplies the expected link matrix; the lab or execution owner supplies target identity and protected WebUI access; the automation owner supplies the browser capture mechanism.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Capture the current source page and enumerate visible Quick-link labels without activating them.
Review UI version, user role and browser console/network errors without clearing BMC or host logs.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not infer or invoke an Identify/UID LED action, click destructive controls, accept cross-host redirects, change BMC settings, clear logs or claim PASS without the expected destination matrix.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Match the approved matrix to the exact firmware/UI and user role, visit every displayed link once, compare each observed result with its expected destination/function, and preserve per-link evidence and exceptions.

revision_candidate.test_name: BMC Inventory and LEDs Page Quick-link Navigation
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify that every Quick link displayed on the BMC WebUI Inventory and LEDs page opens the intended same-target destination or UI function without navigation errors.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact server BMC firmware/UI build, approved user role and supported browser identified by the product specification.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All Quick links rendered under BMC-Web > Hardware Status > Inventory and LEDs for the verified target and role. LED state control is outside scope unless explicitly defined by a future source revision.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Verified BMC/SUT identity; protected WebUI credentials; validated TLS endpoint; compatible browser/UI harness; owner-approved link label/destination/function/permission matrix; evidence location.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Open the specified BMC WebUI page. Capture the complete Quick-link baseline. Activate each displayed Quick link individually, record its resolved page, dialog or resource and confirm it remains on the intended BMC/SUT. Return to the source page between checks. Do not operate controls inside the destination merely to prove the link works.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC, UI version and account role verified; expected matrix available; browser supported; credentials protected; unrelated configuration unchanged; no concurrent BMC update.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity/version/role and timestamp; source-page screenshot; complete displayed link inventory; per-link expected and observed destination/function; same-target result; browser/UI error status; screenshots or structured navigation trace; unresolved or absent links.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The owner-approved BMC firmware/UI Quick-link matrix for this exact product and role, together with the source criterion that all displayed Quick links are workable.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Navigation only. Do not toggle LEDs or other settings, submit forms, accept unapproved external/cross-host redirects, bypass TLS, expose credentials or clear SEL/host logs.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: An owner must approve the expected link matrix and any exception. No state-changing action is authorized by this row.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: A browser agent may navigate and capture results. The BMC/UI owner judges product-specific destinations, role-dependent visibility and intentional exceptions.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On a wrong host, unexpected mutation or destructive destination, stop navigation, preserve browser/BMC audit evidence, close the session and have the owner verify target state. Normal broken links require no target recovery.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Wrong BMC/SUT; missing expected matrix; credential/TLS failure; cross-host or external redirect not approved by the matrix; unexpected write/action; destructive control activation; or inability to capture a per-link result.

identified_defects: DeepSeek substitutes a Redfish LED-control test for a WebUI Quick-link test.
V2 retains unsupported LED-toggle and physical-observation requirements.
The source omits the firmware-specific link/destination matrix and precise meaning of `workable`.
reason_for_change: Restore the exact source operation—checking every WebUI Quick link—and remove the invented LED mutation while preserving destination, identity and evidence controls.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-BMC-00889-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The procedure directs the tester to enter the Inventory and LEDs page and check all Quick links; it does not instruct a LED toggle or a Redfish replacement.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The exact link set and expected destinations are firmware/UI-specific and absent.

removed_ambiguities: Separates link activation from operating controls on the destination page.
Explicitly excludes an inferred LED state test.
Defines per-link same-target and destination evidence.
resolved_blockers: Physical LED observation is no longer treated as a prerequisite for this navigation-only source row.
remaining_blockers: Final verdict needs the exact firmware/UI Quick-link expectation and protected target access.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents a source-invented LED mutation, preserves the mandatory BMC WebUI interface and makes every displayed Quick link independently auditable against a version-specific destination matrix.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Isolated validation confirmed complete per-link BMC WebUI navigation coverage, exact target/UI/browser/role identity, trusted TLS/session scope, one activation per displayed Quick link, return-to-source sequencing, destination controls excluded, same-BMC proof, complete evidence, and no PASS from login, page reachability or a subset of links.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Functionality row 1618 explicitly opens BMC-Web > Hardware Status > Inventory and LEDs and checks all Quick links.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 restores full-link coverage but imports a LED-toggle operation not stated by the row.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Require per-link browser evidence and same-target verification while prohibiting destination-page state changes and invented LED actions.
